newsitem.title: FRANCE: Publicis sees 96 profit rise by 10-15 pct.
newsitem.headline: Publicis sees 96 profit rise by 10-15 pct.

text.p: Advertising group Publicis expects net profit to increase by between 10 and 15 percent in 1996 after jumping 27 percent in 1995 to 152.7 million francs, chairman Maurice Levy said in an interview due for release in the Saturday edition of the Journal des Finances.
"We should be in a position to record, as planned, a profit rise of 10 to 15 percent when compared to 153 million francs last year," he told the French weekly.
Levy denied plans to acquire U.S. group True North, in which Publicis has a 20 percent stake. True North owns 21 percent of Communication, an unlisted unit of Publicis.

He said Publicis had paid True North 50 million francs amounting to dividends left unpaid over several years. The amount will be included in 1996 (accounts) and will have an impact on cash flow but not on earnings, he added.
